explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1212: there is an infinite path in the visible-lattice-point graph (adjacent means differing by ±1 in exactly one coordinate) through vertices with gcd = 1, min(x,y) > 1, and at least one coordinate composite. With both coordinates > 1, 'not prime' is the same as composite. The path is encoded as an injective sequence of adjacent vertices with x + y → ∞. The divergence condition is in fact implied by injectivity, so the statement is faithful. The solved status rests on the linked construction and formalization by Li, which the cached page does not mention.
